newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Miss Hungary re-crowned after six-year battle.
newsitem.headline: Miss Hungary re-crowned after six-year battle.

text.p: Six years almost to the day since she was disqualified as Miss Hungary for having posed naked, beauty queen Antonia Balint was re-awarded her crown on Wednesday after winning a court case against the organisers.
"She's a very courageous girl," said head of the jury Eniko Suto. "I'm delighted to hand her the crown which is rightfully hers."

Balint and second placed Timea Raba were both disqualified immediately after the 1991 pageant when Hungarian newspapers printed photographs that had previously appeared in the men's magazine Lui and other publications.
The incident was one of several problems which beset the early pre-capitalist years of the Miss Hungary contest which started only in 1987 and whose first winner, Csilla Molnar, committed suicide.

Erich Reil, the man who wrote the rules for Miss World, said Balint should hand her prize back. The local organisers, Multimedia Kft, then re-claimed the two contestants' prize money and named third-placed Orsolya Michna as the new Miss Hungary, sending her to the Miss World finals in London.

"I felt it was a huge injustice at the time because there was nothing in the contract I signed which said I'd done anything wrong," Balint told Reuters as she clutched her sceptre to her black velvet dress after Wednesday's award ceremony.
Balint and Raba had signed contracts with Multimedia, which was acting under licence from Miss World in London.
"The rule had been completely mistranslated in the contract we signed with Multimedia," Balint's lawyer Katalin Kiszely explained.

"Instead of the clause about not being allowed to pose nude there was a sentence saying contestants who had done such pictures should not allow other magazines to publish them during the competition."
Balint was to have received a Renault Clio as well but never saw it. She refused to hand over the crown and sceptre and locked them away for six years in her parents' home.

A Budapest court finally ruled this month that Multimedia had misled Balint and awarded her damages plus the price of the Renault car plus interest, estimated at a total $30,000 -- allowing her to take the crown out of storage.
"It's been frustrating not to be able to look at it for six years but I can finally call it mine," she said.
